html: Awaeté ("true people") is the name used for themselves by the Asurini, a Tupi-Guarani-speaking people of the middle Xingu basin in Pará, Brazil. The Asurini of the Xingu live south of the town of Altamira. They had no peaceful contact with Brazilian society until 1971, when missionaries reached them, and new diseases then cut their numbers sharply. They are known for fine geometric body painting, pottery and wood carving. Their land lies upstream of the Belo Monte dam on the Xingu, built in the 2010s. Like other Tupi peoples, they farm cassava and hunt and fish in the forest.
